task3_6_recommendation: Ship the checkpoint/resume patch (verified) and run 4-6 single-threaded workers (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1) with --resume, needing 4-6 GiB free RAM: expected ~4.5-6 h instead of 14-17 h, with zero change to the statistic. That needs a ~5-line --shard i/N flag (deliberately not implemented here); until then the no-code-change split is mpdd|btad (~9-12 h, bounded by btad). The GPU is a genuine ~6-7x on the dominant stage and fits in 3.3 GiB of free VRAM, but it is a rewrite plus a full 1e-6 revalidation - do it separately if the CPU-parallel path is not enough. Cheapest immediate win: reuse the block counts across the two pooling calls (~11%).
uncertainty: the synthetic N=4 aggregate speedup is 2.55x while the real code path measured 3.33x; the truth is somewhere in 3-4x for 4-6 workers and the worker table uses the conservative end
the btad half of the serial wall (9-12 h) is a projection from the first mpdd unit, not a measurement
